headline: Approved $525,000 Early College grant, $81,975.93 in prior-year payments, and 2026-2027 goals for Superintendent Allen.
summary: Members approved the consent agenda, the superintendent's 2026-2027 goals, and several grants and finance items. Proposed changes to the CTE admissions and middle school pathway policies were referred to Operations and Governance. Other items were referred to administration, recommitted, or approved and filed.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including minutes of the September 3, 2026 meeting, donations, and personnel records, 9-0.
Approved the goals and objectives for Superintendent Allen for the 2026-2027 school year, 9-0.
Approved grants and other finance items, including the $525,000 Early College Support Grant and 13 prior-year payments totaling $81,975.93, 9-0.
Recommitted gb 6-23 on the Claremont/Woodland St structure, 9-0.
Approved and filed gb 6-46 on Hispanic/Latinx student enrollment in advanced coursework, 9-0.
Referred gb 6-99 on proposed changes to the CTE Admissions Policy to Operations and Governance, 9-0.
Referred gb 6-100 on proposed changes to the Middle School Pathway Exploration Policy to Operations and Governance, 9-0.
Referred gb 6-101 on National Awareness Days and Months to Administration, 9-0.
Approved and filed gb 6-102 on recognizing May as Mental Health Month, 9-0.
Referred gb 6-103 on cyber security preparedness to Administration, 9-0.
Approved and filed the evaluation report for the School Committee Clerk (gb 6-104), 9-0.

K. Report of the Superintendent  
 ros 6-12 (Administration) 
   (September 17, 2026) 
 WPS Superintendent Goals for School Year 2026-2027  
  
Superintendent Allen presented five goals: one student learning goal, one professional 
practice goal, and three district improvement goals.  
 
The student learning goal is to increase the percentage of students meeting or 
exceeding benchmarks on STAR reading and math assessments from 35% to 38%.  
 
Superintendent Allen will participate in Harvard University's Public Education 
Leadership Program to enhance leadership and organizational coherence as his 
professional practice goal.  
 
For the first district improvement goal, Superintendent Allen will increase the 
percentage of schools with collaborative teams (PLCs, department/grade-level teams 
that consistently implement components for effective collaboration. 
 
The second district improvement goal will be a continuation of the Grow Your Own 
program that began last year. This goal will design and implement a ‘grow your own’ 
school and district leadership pipeline and pathway, inclusive of community 
partnership and concrete pathways. By June 2027, WPS will have completed a new 
principal leadership cohort, a new instructional coach pipeline, and a new assistant 
principal / Dean pipeline. 
 
The third district improvement goal is the second year of a multi year goal for school 
boundary realignment. A comprehensive analysis of the school boundaries is currently

under way.  
Member Mailman asked  Superintendent Allen if he considered any other student 
learning goal. Superintendent Allen stated that STAR data is an accurate 
representation of student achievement and a predictor of MCAS Success. He feels this 
is the best way to measure student achievement at this time.  
 
Member Mailman asked how a review of curriculum selection fits into a student 
learning goal and asked Superintendent Allen to consider curriculum selection in the 
future.  
 
A motion was made to approve the goals and objectives for Superintendent 
Allen for the 2026-2027 school year. On a voice vote of 9-0 the motion 
passed unanimously.

gb 6-46 (Alvarez)  
  (April 16, 2026) 
Response from Administration for gb 6-46 
Request data on enrollment and participation of Hispanic/Latinx students in advanced 
coursework and recommend actions to increase access and support as needed. 
 
Member Alvarez noted the report had a lot of helpful information. She mentioned that 
Latino students make up half of our student population and the data presented shows 
that our Latino students are more than capable of taking on and doing well in AP 
courses and other advanced coursework. She also noted the lack of enrollment of 
Latino students in courses outside of AP Spanish.  
 
Member Mailman asked Superintendent Allen  if there is an opportunity to target 
recruiting Latino students to take AP and advanced courses. Superintendent Allen 
said this is going to be a focus of the district this year. As a board member at LEI, 
Superintendent Allen is committed to increasing the number of Latino students who 
enroll in advanced coursework. 
 
Member Binienda mentioned that the College Board data shows that Latino students 
who take Spanish first, then take Spanish Literature generally move on to participate 
in a larger variety of advanced coursework. 
 
A motion was made to approve and file this item. On a voice vote of 9-0, the 
motion passed unanimously.  
 
gb 6-99 (Administration) 
   (September 17, 2026) 
 Proposed Changes to CTE Admissions Policy 
 To Approve the Proposed Changes to the Career Technical Education Admissions 
Policy for 2026-2027. 
 
 Member Biancheria asked if eighth grade students have an opportunity to see what is 
offered in our high schools. She recommends that students also look at what is being 
offered at their home high school, in addition to other programs, specifically 
Worcester Tech. She also asked how we advertise what Worcester Tech offers. Dr. 
Emily Lehman, Administrative Director of College & Career Readiness, noted that 
offerings are sent to all eighth grade families through Parent Square and during the 
enrollment process. She noted that seventh graders were also offered “career days” 
to help inform decision making once the student gets to grade eight.  
 
Member Biancheria made a motion requesting the administration look at 
offering open houses at various schools on varying dates, including 
E. Approval of Minutes - 9.17.26
Page 6 
Saturdays. 
 
 Member Mailman agreed with Member Biancheria’s motion. She also noted that WPS 
is doing a great job in making the WTHS lottery more equitable, as it brings stronger 
programming to students from all neighborhoods.  
  
 A motion was made to refer this item to Operations and Governance. On a 
voice vote of 9-0, the motion passed unanimously.  
 
 gb 6-100 (Administration) 
   (September 17, 2026) 
 Proposed Changes to Middle School Pathway Exploration Policy 
 To Approve the Proposed Changes to the Middle School Pathway Exploration Policy  
for 2026-2027. 
  
 Member Biancheria noted that WPS needs to improve in Middle School Pathways for 
North High School. Superintendent Allen said that the North Quadrant is a focus area 
to expand CTE offerings at North High School. The administration is actively working 
on these offerings and will be mapping out some of those plans soon. There will be  
an update this spring.  
 
 A motion was made to refer this item to Operations and Governance. On a 
voice vote of 9-0, the motion passed unanimously.

  (September 17, 2026)

gb 6-102 (Roy)  
  (September 17, 2026)

promoting mental health education and resources. 
 
Member Roy noted that this topic is close to her heart. She respectfully requests this 
item be approved.

gb 6-103 (Mailman)  
(September 17, 2026) 
Request administration share how the district is prepared to keep WPS open and 
operational during a cyber security incident, including day to day operational items, 
such as attendance and buses.  
 
Member Mailman presented her item. As a result of what transpired in Springfield, 
MA, Member Mailman requests that WPS performs an audit so we can react quickly if 
a cyberattack should happen. Superintendent Allen noted that WPS’s IT department 
has been in touch with Springfield to offer support.  
 
A motion was made to refer this item to Administration. On a voice vote of 
9-0, the motion passed unanimously.
